clue.text: Push through deep exit frenetically

indicators.note: doing something frenetically means doing it wildly, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone rushes frantically towards a deep exit, pushing through a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: To expedite a matter is to hurry it along, a synonym of pushing it through.

clue.text: Site of mausoleum consumed in conflagration

indicators.note: what is consumed in something is swallowed up inside it, so look within the next word

blocks.note: sits inside this word, from its third letter

explanation.surface: A mausoleum is destroyed in a great fire.
explanation.walkthrough: The mausoleum is the Taj Mahal, which stands in the Indian city of Agra.
explanation.definitionFit: The Taj Mahal, the world's most famous mausoleum, is located in this city in Uttar Pradesh.

clue.text: Damage politician in one broadcast

indicators.note: one thing set in another goes inside it, so the politician sits within the rest

blocks.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: A politician does himself harm in a single broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair something is to weaken or harm it, a synonym of damage as a verb.

clue.text: Disorganised nonsense in note

indicators.note: the nonsense is placed in the following word, inside its letters

blocks.note: to note is to observe, to spy

explanation.surface: A written note is full of disorganised nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' is the verb, to notice, not a written message.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrappy work is untidy and poorly organised, made up of bits and pieces.

clue.text: Is interrupting the speaker about repeated plea for mercy

indicators.note: something interrupting another breaks into its middle, so it is set inside

blocks.note: the person speaking refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A plea for mercy keeps interrupting someone giving a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: The Miserere is named from the Latin opening of Psalm 51; 'repeated' tells you to write the previous piece twice.
explanation.definitionFit: The Miserere is Psalm 51, 'Have mercy upon me', so the name stands for a prayer seeking compassion.

clue.text: Piano then fiddle I learnt as composer

indicators.note: to fiddle with something is to tamper with it, rearranging its letters

explanation.surface: A music student learnt piano and then violin on the way to becoming a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle' looks like the violin, matching the piano, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Pierluigi da Palestrina was a leading Italian Renaissance writer of sacred music.

clue.text: Accommodation that subsumes second accommodation

indicators.note: to subsume is to take within, so the following piece goes inside

explanation.surface: A lodging that contains a second set of lodgings within it.
explanation.walkthrough: Both ends of the clue say accommodation: the first is the definition, the second the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostel is cheap shared lodging, a kind of place to stay.

clue.text: Test one conservative holding back effort diversifying unions

definitions.note: an adjective phrase: describing marriages that widen the gene pool

indicators.note: one word holding another keeps it inside its letters
going back means read from right to left

explanation.surface: A political test of one Tory resisting efforts to make trade unions more varied.
explanation.definitionFit: Exogamy is marriage outside one's own tribe or group, which mixes the population.

clue.text: Shakespearean villain trapping maiden for mature monarch, say

indicators.note: a word trapping something holds it captive inside

blocks.note: the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A villain from Shakespeare holds a young woman captive on behalf of an elderly king.
explanation.walkthrough: The monarch is the butterfly, not a king.
explanation.definitionFit: An imago is the final adult stage of an insect, such as a full-grown monarch butterfly.

clue.text: Isolated high point providing some satisfaction, but only some

indicators.note: the phrase that follows supplies the letters from within itself
only part of the phrase is used, a run of letters straddling its words

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A lone peak gives a climber some satisfaction, but only a little.
explanation.definitionFit: A mesa is a flat-topped hill standing apart from the surrounding land, common in the American Southwest.

clue.text: A low place for bargaining is producing indignities

blocks.note: a bargain basement is the cut-price floor of a store

explanation.surface: A cheap downstairs shop is where shoppers suffer humiliations.
explanation.walkthrough: A bargain basement is the lowest floor of a department store where cheap goods are sold.
explanation.definitionFit: Abasements are humiliations or degradations, a plural synonym of indignities.

clue.text: Rubbish that queen may have to bear

definitions.text: that queen may have to bear

blocks.clueFragment: that queen may have to bear
blocks.note: second meaning: a brood of kittens, since a queen is a female cat

explanation.walkthrough: The queen looks royal and 'bear' looks like endure, but a queen is a breeding female cat and to bear is to give birth.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both scattered refuse and a set of young animals born together.

clue.text: Blue Danube is in this outing – hired Brendan in two cases

blocks.note: property let out is hired out
the setter refers to himself as I in the subject case and me in the object case

explanation.surface: The setter hires a boat on the Danube for a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: Brendan is the setter, so he is I or me; 'two cases' are grammatical cases, not luggage.
explanation.definitionFit: The Blue Danube is a waltz, written in three beats to the bar.

clue.text: Run in without importance in attractive fashion

indicators.note: the run is placed in the following phrase, inside its letters

explanation.surface: Instructions to run in casually, as if it does not matter, but gracefully.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something prettily means doing it in a pleasing, charming manner.

clue.text: Condemned left-winger embracing what's wrong

indicators.note: to embrace is to wrap the arms around, so one word goes inside the other

explanation.surface: A leftist politician was denounced for embracing wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: To be reviled is to be attacked with abuse, close in sense to being denounced.

clue.text: Twice daily event for island set up, open to change

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means raised, so the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the sea comes in twice a day

explanation.surface: An event held twice a day for an island community is being organised.
explanation.definitionFit: A text that is editable can be revised or amended, open to alteration.

clue.text: Take to house from food store very shortly

indicators.note: cut short, so the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Groceries are to be taken home from the shop very soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortly' looks like 'soon', but it trims the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver goods is to bring them to a home or address.

clue.text: Kind of blue, counterpart of shocking pink?

blocks.note: first meaning: a vivid, steely blue shade
second meaning: a word for giving a jolt, as shocking does

explanation.walkthrough: Shocking pink is a real colour name; the matching adjective that also means delivering a jolt names a vivid blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Electric blue is a bright metallic hue, and electric parallels shocking since electricity shocks.

clue.text: Supply again includes assorted parts for rockets

indicators.note: assorted parts are mixed up, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A resupply shipment includes a mixed bag of spare parts for rockets.
explanation.definitionFit: To restock shelves is to refill them, providing a fresh supply.

clue.text: Guided a returning assistant in state capital

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so these words are read in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: A tour guide returns with an assistant in a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Adelaide is the capital of the Australian state of South Australia.

clue.text: Be upset when trapped by girlfriend in argument

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters run the other way
something trapped by another is caught inside it

explanation.surface: Someone is distressed at being cornered by a girlfriend during a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A debate is a formal discussion of opposing views, a sense of argument.

clue.text: Made call that's failed without a line

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the first word surrounds the rest

blocks.note: an engine that died has failed

explanation.surface: A phone call was made that failed because there was no line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' seems to mean lacking, which suits a dead phone, but here it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Dialed, the American spelling of dialled, means placed a phone call by entering a number.

clue.text: Scrambled draw at home – he considered selection, naturally

indicators.note: scrambled letters are jumbled into a different order

explanation.surface: After a scrappy home draw, the manager naturally thought about team selection.
explanation.walkthrough: The football picture misleads: 'selection, naturally' is natural selection.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Darwin developed the theory of evolution by natural selection.

clue.text: Person whose job is summarising a short book or penning small treatise

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, as in a sheep pen, so the outer letters wrap around the rest

explanation.surface: A description of someone who condenses a short book or writes a brief essay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penning' looks like writing, which suits the surface, but it means enclosing, as a sheep pen does.
explanation.definitionFit: An abstractor writes abstracts, brief summaries of documents or legal titles.

clue.text: Creative efforts are raising the stakes, first of all

indicators.note: the opening letter of every one of the words is taken

explanation.surface: Creative work is becoming more of a gamble.
explanation.definitionFit: The arts are creative pursuits like painting, music and literature.

clue.text: It's said to accompany a will from home

definitions.text: It's said to accompany a will

blocks.clueFragment: It's said to accompany a will
blocks.note: first meaning: the proverb holds that where there's a will there's one of these
second meaning: absent, not at home

explanation.walkthrough: 'It's said' points to a saying, not a sound-alike: the proverb pairs a will with a way. 'Will' is not a legal document here.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-word phrase from the proverb also forms the adverb meaning absent, as in an away match.

clue.text: Perhaps Indian Mutiny's leader imprisoned in end

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its front letter
something imprisoned in another is shut up inside it

explanation.surface: The leader of the Indian Mutiny was jailed in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The Indian Mutiny of 1857 looks like one historical event, but 'Indian' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tamil is a member of a people of southern India and Sri Lanka, so an example of an Indian.

clue.text: Reaching crescendo without middle C, like Four Seasons' variations

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the named letter is dropped

blocks.note: the C standing in the middle of the word

explanation.surface: Music building to a climax, but without middle C, like variations in Vivaldi's Four Seasons.
explanation.walkthrough: Middle C looks like the piano note, but it is the C in the middle of the longer word.
explanation.definitionFit: Vivaldi's Four Seasons depicts the weather of each season, so its variations are of the weather kind.
